comments.author: @ThePlanetDocumentary
comments.text: There is something special about islands shaped by volcanic activity. The Azores have such a unique character, from their rugged landscapes to their peaceful atmosphere. This documentary makes me want to explore every island someday.

comments.author: @joseabreu3628
comments.text: Açores dos meus amores. I love S.MIGUEL.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: É fácil perceber porque é que São Miguel ocupa um lugar tão especial no teu coração, @joseabreu3628! A beleza desta ilha permanece na memória muito tempo depois de ter partido. Obrigado por assistir!

comments.author: @josephrego2527
comments.text: There are many earthquakes yearly, possibly closer to 4,000. Most, thankfully, so small, they aren't even noticed.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That’s a really helpful detail to add, @josephrego2527! Living with that constant, quiet volcanic activity underneath is what makes the Azores so geographically unique.

comments.author: @MelodyScape-hm
comments.text: The landscapes here look almost unreal.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: The Azores definitely have an otherworldly vibe, @Worldtravel-f4e. We're so glad we could share that "unreal" beauty with you through our 4K lens!

comments.author: @pualeiquintagrande6309
comments.text: Blonde hair? Never knew a Portuguese being that blonde

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Portugal and the Atlantic islands actually have a very diverse genetic history, @pualeiquintagrande6309! It’s one of those interesting facts that often surprises visitors. Thanks for watching!

comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: The scenery is incredible, but beautiful isolation can feel very different once it becomes everyday life.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That’s a very insightful point, @LifewaysTravel. The reality of remote living is often much more complex than what the camera captures in a documentary. Thanks for sharing that perspective!

comments.author: @brigidspencer5123
comments.text: My family is from the Azores. We have visited Sao Miguel frequently with our kids. Iceland is connected under the ocean to the volcanic Azores. Any area located on tectonic plates shakes frequently.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: It’s fascinating to hear about your family's connection to Sao Miguel, @brigidspencer5123. That geological link between Iceland and the Azores is truly a powerful reminder of how connected our planet is.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We’re so glad you enjoyed the stunning scenery of this paradise!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: It’s truly impressive to see how they've adapted to life in the middle of the Atlantic, @thegatesofdawn...1386. Their ingenuity is a huge part of what makes the Azores so special!

comments.author: @thegatesofdawn...1386
comments.text:
Why did the Portuguese move from the mainland to the Azore Islands.
Tough people.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: They truly are resilient people, @thegatesofdawn...1386. Most moved centuries ago seeking new opportunities and fertile land. Thanks for watching!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: It truly is a spectacular place to witness, @PlanetsDiscover! We're glad you enjoyed the authentic feel of the film.

comments.author: @LifeinImpossiblePlaces69
comments.text: The Azores feel like the kind of place that quietly reminds you life doesn't have to move so fast. Living on isolated volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic can't be easy, yet the people seem to have built a life that's both resilient and deeply fulfilling. I'd choose an experience like this over a crowded resort any day.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We completely agree; there is something so special and restorative about the slower, more intentional pace of life found on these islands. 🌋

comments.author: @GracaSantos-lu7yv
comments.text: Açores ,o paraíso na terra! A mãe natureza ,bafejou estas ilhas de uma beleza extraordinária! Já tive a sorte de visitar S. Miguel e voltarei um dia à Terceira! ADOREI!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Os Açores são verdadeiramente uma obra-prima da natureza, @GracaSantos-lu7yv! Que bom que já conhece São Miguel e esperamos que possa visitar a Terceira em breve. Obrigada por partilhar o seu amor pelas ilhas!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We’re always looking for ways to improve our storytelling, so thank you for your honest thoughts on the commentary.
